page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based server instance belonging to the Epsv6 family. It is powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture is arm64, with a cache configuration consisting of 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved top-tier results in large-block memory bandwidth tests, with read-only speeds of 436.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 184.19 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and memory scores also placed in the top tier. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. However, single-core performance remains average, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores in the middle tier. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model scoring in the bottom tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32ps_v6 offers high memory density and dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, which reduces resource contention. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-effective option for memory-intensive workloads that rely on network-attached premium storage. Based on its top-tier database operations and memory bandwidth, this server is suited for database hosting, memory-intensive web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks, while being less suitable for heavy single-threaded execution or large-scale AI model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized server instance powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 32 vCPUs, and 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks bundled local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and database operations, alongside strong multi-core processing capabilities. Conversely, single-core performance and large-scale LLM inference speeds are average to poor. This hardware profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-dense workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. It is best suited for database hosting, multi-threaded data processing, and high-throughput web serving.
